transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Ever since my husband’s stroke, I just haven’t been handling everything the way I usually do, and I feel like I’m not coping with all these changes. My daughter really encouraged me to come in and talk to someone because it's all been so different lately.
Can you tell me more about how you've been feeling since your husband's stroke, specifically any feelings of sadness, guilt, or anxiety that have been bothering you?

I feel constantly on edge and worn thin, and I lie awake at night worrying that I'm failing my husband and letting everything else fall apart. I've even found myself snapping at my dear friends from church, which makes me feel terribly guilty because I'm just not coping well.
Can you tell me more about when these feelings of being on edge and guilty started, was it immediately after your husband's stroke or did they develop over time?

It didn't start the very day of his stroke, but rather a week or two after I brought him home from the hospital. That was when all the daily caregiving routines, medication schedules, and doctor appointments really started piling up and fell entirely on my shoulders. That's when I truly started feeling so overwhelmed and on edge.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning, such as avoiding social interactions or having difficulty managing daily tasks, since your husband's stroke?

Yes, I really have been struggling to keep up with my daily life. I've had to back out of leading our church potluck and missed several choir rehearsals, and I've even missed paying a couple of bills on time because I'm just too overwhelmed to keep track of everything.
Have your feelings of being on edge, guilt, and overwhelm been present every day since they started, or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better or back to your normal self?

They have been pretty much constant every single day since I brought my husband home from the hospital. I haven't really had any breaks or times where I felt back to my normal self, because I just feel constantly on edge and overwhelmed by it all.
Can you tell me if these feelings of being on edge and overwhelmed have lasted for more than two weeks, and if you've had any significant periods where they seemed to lessen or worsen over time?

Yes, they have been going on for about a month now, which is definitely more than two weeks. They haven't really lessened at all because the daily caregiving demands and doctor appointments have been completely continuous.

Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment that seems to be directly in response to your husband's stroke and the resulting caregiving responsibilities, and if so, has this distress been persistent over the past month?

Yes, this distress is completely tied to my husband's stroke and trying to handle all his caregiving needs on my own. It has been constant for the past month, leaving me feeling on edge, snapping at my church friends, and failing to pay bills or keep up with my choir commitments.

You mentioned that your symptoms started about a month ago, can you tell me if you've experienced any intrusive memories, thoughts, or dreams related to your husband's stroke, or if your symptoms are more focused on the ongoing stress of caregiving?

No, I haven't had any intrusive memories or bad dreams about the stroke itself. My struggles are entirely focused on the daily stress of caregiving, like keeping track of his medications and appointments, and just feeling so overwhelmed by these new responsibilities.

You've mentioned that your symptoms are entirely focused on the daily stress of caregiving for your husband, but can you tell me if you've experienced any significant anxiety or fear related to your own health or the possibility of something similar happening to you or another loved one?

No, I haven't really thought about my own health or feared something like that happening to me. All of my worry and anxiety have been entirely focused on managing my husband's care, making sure I don't fail him, and trying to keep up with my daily responsibilities.

Is it possible for you to imagine or experience a significant reduction in your feelings of being on edge and overwhelmed if the caregiving responsibilities for your husband were to be significantly alleviated or shared with others?

Yes, I definitely think reducing that burden would help me immensely. In fact, the social worker at the clinic reassured me that once my husband becomes more independent and these caregiving demands slow down, this overwhelming phase should settle down within a few months. I'm really hoping that's the case so I can start feeling like myself again.

If the caregiving responsibilities for your husband were to be significantly alleviated or shared with others, do you think your feelings of being on edge and overwhelmed would decrease substantially within a short period, such as a few weeks, or would they likely take longer to improve?

I think I would feel some relief pretty quickly, but it would probably take a few months to completely get back to normal. The social worker told me that once my husband is more independent and the caregiving slows down, this rough patch should settle down within a few months rather than dragging on. So I expect it would take about that long to fully resolve.
